what: The robot combines colour measurements with wheel motion to explore a marked surface. Use colour feedback and heading to reach a target on the floor.
try: Run the supplied example on its colour-zone mat.
Observe where the colour sensor points when a decision changes the motion.
Reset and change one colour-dependent action in the code.
why: A colour measurement describes the patch beneath the sensor, not the whole robot. A program turns that local observation into a navigation decision.
matters: This is a simple form of event-driven autonomous navigation.
question: Will a colour change happen as soon as a wheel reaches the patch?
answer: Only when the sensor’s own footprint reaches it. Its offset from the wheels matters.
further: Compare a sensor event with the drive-axle position.
Try reflected-light control along a line.
